answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and slash that stake when peers prove fraud. An honest agent pays once and recovers it through good work, while an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand separate stakes, so cost rises with each fake. This is no ivory-tower rule: the stake is the summit a newcomer must reach before earning trust, and like yarrow, fake identities can only spread where each new shoot has been planted and paid for.
